record_type_quote: The current study extends the validity and replicability of the BCEs scale with a second high-risk sample: parents of young children residing at an urban emergency homeless shelter.

targets.authors: Narayan AJ, Rivera LM, Bernstein RE, Harris WW, & Lieberman AF
targets.title: Positive childhood experiences predict less psychopathology and stress in pregnant women with childhood adversity: A pilot study of the benevolent childhood experiences (BCEs) scale.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly identify matching BCE frequencies with one differing item. They also align psychological distress prediction with the pilot while explaining a discrepant contextual-stress association: BCEs predicted stressful life events in the pilot but not contextual stress here. There is no overall replication-success verdict overriding these differences. Parenting stress is an extension. ACEs literature comparisons are background rather than separately designed retests.

reasoning: Independent homeless-parent sample tests the published pilot findings on BCE distributions and prediction of mental health and contextual stress. Identity verified against title and all four authors.
